{"id":"74d2d5e3-afe9-48d2-bef3-64741d2a5a60","state":"COMPLETED","response":"# Independent adversarial audit of Erdős #99, notes §§32–45

Verdict: the principal arguments are mathematically coherent within their stated hypotheses, but several implications require careful qualification. I found no demonstrated resolution of Erdős #99 and no counterexample invalidating the central theorems. The strongest useful conclusion from this audit is a combined normal form for selected hypothetical triangle-free global optimizers. The main outstanding issue is the absence of a theorem that turns geometric size, cyclic rigidity, or large diameter-cover number into sufficient contact density or a strict diameter improvement.

This is an independent proof audit, not formal verification. I have treated assertions about earlier computational and worker checks as provenance, not mathematical evidence. The original problem remains open. Erdős Problems

## 1. Cross-component diameter release and its structural consequence (§§32, 42)

Let AAA be finite and unit-separated, with diameter DDD, and let GGG be its complete unit-contact graph.

The claim that all cross-component actual diameter pairs admit simultaneous strict shortening by componentwise translations withstands the following check.

For a cross-component diameter pair pqpqpq, define

Lpq(v)=(p−q)⋅(vC(p)−vC(q)).L_{pq}(v)=(p-q)\cdot(v_{C(p)}-v_{C(q)}).Lpq​(v)=(p−q)⋅(vC(p)​−vC(q)​).

If no vvv makes every Lpq(v)<0L_{pq}(v)<0Lpq​(v)<0, Gordan's alternative supplies nonzero nonnegative weights on cross-component diameter pairs balancing the resultant force on every contact component.

Every loaded diameter endpoint is an exposed vertex of the convex hull. The loaded vertices belonging to different contact components form a noncrossing partition: alternating boundary vertices would require their disjoint unit-contact paths to intersect. A noncrossing partition with multiple blocks has a consecutive proper block. Such a block can be strictly separated from the other loaded endpoints, making every incident weighted cross-diameter force have the same strict projection sign. This contradicts componentwise balance.

The collinear case reduces to the unique diameter pair. Finite inactive-constraint slack converts the translation velocities into genuine small feasible motions.

Therefore:

1. Every ordinary local diameter minimum has at least one diameter pair internal to a full contact component.
2. At most one full contact component can contain an internal diameter pair, because distinct diameter segments with four endpoints must cross.
3. A triangle-free global optimizer selected by lexicographically minimizing (β,c,k)(\beta,c,k)(β,c,k) has all actual diameter pairs inside one full contact component, where kkk counts actual diameter pairs.

There is a useful additional interaction with §42:

Combined normal-form consequence. In that (β,c,k)(\beta,c,k)(β,c,k)-minimal representative, every other full contact component is a tree.

Indeed, such a component contains no actual diameter endpoint. A small dilation about its centroid strictly opens all its unit contacts while leaving every actual diameter unchanged. If the component contained a cycle, this would decrease β=M−n+c\beta=M-n+cβ=M−n+c, contradicting first-stage minimality.

This is a partial structural theorem, not a connectedness theorem. It is compatible with the near-full component circumradii from §31 and does not control the total mass of the detached trees.

Crucially, the alternative eDe_DeD​-maximizing normal form in §30 cannot be appended to this conclusion. The two secondary optimization rules need not have a common representative.

## 2. A decisive incompatibility between cyclic locking, packet folds, and Dines (§§36, 42, 45)

This is an important vacuity result not explicitly emphasized in the notes.

Assume simultaneously that the representative minimizes β\betaβ and its entire contact graph is a simply connected rhombic disk. Let TTT be its number of train tracks, and let

F:RT⟶R2k,F(a)i=J∑tεitatutF:\mathbb R^T\longrightarrow\mathbb R^{2k}, \qquad F(a)_i=J\sum_t\varepsilon_{it}a_tu_tF:RT⟶R2k,F(a)i​=Jt∑​εit​at​ut​

record first-order changes of actual diameter vectors.

Every rhombic-disk edge belongs to a contact cycle. Cycle-rank minimality therefore gives

ker⁡F={0}.\ker F=\{0\}.kerF={0}.

Proof. If F(a)=0F(a)=0F(a)=0, the track-angle infinitesimal motion preserves all actual diameter vectors. Cyclic locking makes the relative velocity on every contact edge zero. But a track-edge vector has derivative atJuta_tJu_tat​Jut​, forcing every at=0a_t=0at​=0.

Consequently:

T≤2k,b=2T≤4k,T\le2k,\qquad b=2T\le4k,T≤2k,b=2T≤4k,

and Euler gives

M=2n−2−T≥2n−2−2k.M=2n-2-T\ge2n-2-2k.M=2n−2−T≥2n−2−2k.

These are valid only for a complete rhombic-contact disk.

More importantly, the same hypotheses make the quadratic kernel KDK_DKD​ in §45 zero-dimensional. Dines's two-form alternative remains mathematically correct, but its negative-semidefinite branch becomes automatic and supplies no obstruction.

Likewise, the nonzero balanced packets required for §36 cannot exist in this selected full-disk representative: they would produce nonzero vectors in ker⁡F\ker FkerF.

Thus §§36, 42 and 45 must not be treated as three independently accumulating rigidity gains on one representative. The packet and Dines methods may be useful for different representatives or broader frameworks, but cyclic locking already eliminates their relevant first-order kernel here.

The bridge generalization is narrower. If bbrb_{\rm br}bbr​ denotes the number of bridges in the full contact graph, deleting bridges leaves c+bbrc+b_{\rm br}c+bbr​ cyclic-edge components. Rank-nullity gives

M+2k≥2(n−c−bbr),M+2k\ge2(n-c-b_{\rm br}),M+2k≥2(n−c−bbr​),

or

M≥2n−2c−2bbr−2k.M\ge2n-2c-2b_{\rm br}-2k.M≥2n−2c−2bbr​−2k.

This deduction checks out. The missing premise remains bbr=O(D)b_{\rm br}=O(D)bbr​=O(D); the notes do not establish it.

The underlying rhombic framework uses Kenyon–Schlenker's train-track structure, while the convexity of the image of two quadratic forms is due to Dines (1941). The latter is supported by the original [Dines article](https://projecteuclid.org/journals/bulletin-of-the-american-mathematical-society/volume-47/issue-6/On-the-mapping-of-quadratic-forms/bams/1183503694.short?utm_source=chatgpt.com). Neither source proves the global full-disk premise.

## 3. Degree-two local minima, internal loading and the n≤9n\le9n≤9 threshold (§§33, 38–39)

The chain is credible, subject to the strict infinitesimal Carpenter's Rule theorem rather than merely its continuous-motion version.

Connelly–Demaine–Rote prove the required expansive infinitesimal motion after handling straight runs, convex cycles and nested components. Their restrictions matter: the theorem cannot simply be applied to an arbitrary overlapping linkage. erikdemaine.org

For a local minimum with complete contact maximum degree two, §33's cycle-closure argument supplies the additional step: a straight diametral run of mmm unit links with angular rates aja_jaj​ satisfies

∣∑jej(t)∣2=m2−t2∑i<j(ai−aj)2+o(t2).\left|\sum_j e_j(t)\right|^2 =m^2-t^2\sum_{i<j}(a_i-a_j)^2+o(t^2).​j∑​ej​(t)​2=m2−t2i<j∑​(ai​−aj​)2+o(t2).

A closure-preserving choice with nonconstant rates strictly shortens every exceptional flat run. Thus a convex contact cycle must itself span DDD.

Nearby-local inheritance is valid only because local minimality is ordinary, not strict. Choose an open neighborhood in which every feasible configuration has diameter at least DDD. Moving a non-diameter-active cycle vertex slightly to open its two contacts produces another diameter-DDD configuration inside this neighborhood. A smaller neighborhood of that new configuration inherits local minimality. The spanning cycle has been broken, contradicting §33. Therefore every vertex on the spanning cycle is an actual diameter endpoint, and the cycle is strictly convex.

The positive-loading enhancement requires another argument. For a normalized KKT stress, use the CDR expansive velocity on its positive-contact support. Virtual work forces every positive diameter to belong to a straight positive path or a common convex positive cycle. The straight-path possibility is excluded by strict convexity and the uniqueness of the full diameter-bearing component. Consequently the positive cycle is the entire spanning cycle. Every cycle edge is positively stressed, and equilibrium at a strictly convex vertex forces an internal positive diameter partner.

This is stronger than actual diameter activity, and it does not follow from KKT alone.

The §39 geometric improvement also passes the essential algebra. For a genuine unit hull side and its internal diameter partners, the exterior tangent wedge has apex angle ϕ\phiϕ satisfying

sin⁡(ϕ/2)≥3D2−2D−12D.\sin(\phi/2)\ge \frac{\sqrt{3D^2-2D-1}}{2D}.sin(ϕ/2)≥2D3D2−2D−1​​.

Every point of this wedge is within 1/(2sin⁡(ϕ/2))1/(2\sin(\phi/2))1/(2sin(ϕ/2)) of a side endpoint. Hence exterior diameter-completion points have vertex distance at most

ρ(D)=D3D2−2D−1<1\rho(D)=\frac{D}{\sqrt{3D^2-2D-1}}<1ρ(D)=3D2−2D−1​D​<1

when D>(1+3)/2D>(1+\sqrt3)/2D>(1+3​)/2.

The threshold is automatic for genuine convex unit-sided polygons with at least four vertices: D≥2D\ge\sqrt2D≥2​ for a quadrilateral, while D≥m/πD\ge m/\piD≥m/π for m≥5m\ge5m≥5.

Counterexample to weakening the genuine-side condition. Take the six boundary vertices of the rectangle [0,2]×[−1,0][0,2]\times[-1,0][0,2]×[−1,0], including both horizontal side midpoints. Its diameter is 5\sqrt55​, and all four extreme corners have internal diameter partners. Yet z=(1,1)z=(1,1)z=(1,1) belongs to its diameter completion and has minimum distance exactly one from the six vertices. Collinear subdivisions therefore invalidate strict completion coverage.

With genuine sides restored, §39's nested-component absorption gives A=CA=CA=C for the selected triangle-free global representative of maximum contact degree two. Hence n≤πDn\le\pi Dn≤πD. The strict disk-count inequality n>aD2+1n>aD^2+1n>aD2+1 then implies

n2<2π3(n−1),n^2<2\pi\sqrt3(n-1),n2<2π3​(n−1),

which fails for every integer n≥10n\ge10n≥10.

Assessment: the selected-representative conclusion—contact degree at least three for n≥10n\ge10n≥10—is supported by this dependency chain. It is not a conclusion about every unselected optimizer.

## 4. Strict disk counting and terminal forest retraction (§§35, 40)

The strict improvement n>aDn2+1n>aD_n^2+1n>aDn2​+1 has a sound elementary proof.

Count translates of the unit triangular lattice inside the open disk of radius Dn/2D_n/2Dn​/2. Every translate contains at most n−1n-1n−1 sites; otherwise an nnn-point set would have diameter strictly below DnD_nDn​. The mean count is aDn2aD_n^2aDn2​. The count is not almost everywhere constant: cross a translated lattice point through the disk boundary at a center avoiding all simultaneous boundary crossings. Counts on adjacent open sets differ by one. An integer-valued nonconstant count has mean strictly below its maximum, proving the inequality.

For §40, let xxx be a diameter-endpoint leaf, with degree-two non-diametral neighbor qqq and fixed grandparent ppp. Retract xxx toward ppp, choosing q(t)q(t)q(t) from the intersecting unit circles. The middle joint may move by O(t)O(\sqrt t)O(t​); a differentiable joint motion is unnecessary. It is essential, however, that qqq is not diameter-active.

For simultaneously retractable leaves, put ux=x−pu_x=x-pux​=x−p, or zero for an unretracted endpoint. The diameter inequality gives

2(x−y)⋅ux≥∣ux∣2,2(x-y)\cdot u_x\ge |u_x|^2,2(x−y)⋅ux​≥∣ux​∣2,

and its counterpart at yyy. Therefore

∣x(t)−y(t)∣2≤D2−t2(∣ux∣2+∣uy∣2)|x(t)-y(t)|^2 \le D^2-\frac t2(|u_x|^2+|u_y|^2)∣x(t)−y(t)∣2≤D2−2t​(∣ux​∣2+∣uy​∣2)

for 0<t≤1/40<t\le1/40<t≤1/4.

The arms have disjoint movable vertices under the stated branching hypotheses. Sharing a fixed grandparent causes no interference; sharing a movable degree-two joint would force a path component without branching.

Thus a local minimum must retain a diameter pair avoiding every safely retractable endpoint. The branch-core estimate

D≤2+diam⁡(B)D\le2+\operatorname{diam}(B)D≤2+diam(B)

is valid only with the specified forest, diameter-leaf and branching assumptions.

Dropping the joint-inactivity condition is demonstrably unsafe: the exact rational example in §40 gives a derivative +9/10+9/10+9/10 for the squared length of a diameter incident to the moving joint. This defeats that retraction, not the conditional theorem. erdos99-verified-notes.md

## 5. Stress countermodels and geometric sharpness (§§34, 41, 43)

These constructions obstruct three different shortcuts.

The four-arm example in §34 has a nonnegative branching-tree equilibrium stress, k=2k=2k=2, exact disk radius D/2D/2D/2, bounded hull-area deficit and optimal leading density. Nevertheless, explicitly rotating terminal links shortens both diameters. Its cardinality also violates the necessary global inequality. Therefore it is neither locally nor globally optimal.

The two interdigitated combs in §43 have exactly two full contact trees, each extending almost to the enclosing radius. Their hull is nearly circular and both trees participate in its boundary. This refutes geometry-only implications from near-roundness and macroscopic component size to connectedness. It does not refute a theorem assuming local minimality or a global optimality certificate.

The constant-width construction in §41 addresses sharpness of the geometric diameter-degree estimate. With R=D/2R=D/2R=D/2 and b=D−1/3b=D^{-1/3}b=D−1/3, its C1,1C^{1,1}C1,1 support function has

h(θ)+h(θ+π)=D,h+h′′∈{0,R,D}a.e.h(\theta)+h(\theta+\pi)=D,\qquad h+h''\in\{0,R,D\}\quad\text{a.e.}h(θ)+h(θ+π)=D,h+h′′∈{0,R,D}a.e.

The required matching of first derivatives prevents curvature atoms at the piecewise junctions. Hynd's support-function criterion then establishes an actual constant-width convex body, rather than merely a formal candidate. BPB

The opposite circular arc supplies Θ(D2/3)\Theta(D^{2/3})Θ(D2/3) unit-separated points all at distance DDD from one corner. The area loss is O(D)O(D)O(D), and a cleared, slightly expanded triangular-lattice filler gives a finite triangle-free set of cardinality aD2+O(D)aD^2+O(D)aD2+O(D).

This supports sharpness of

ΔD=O(D2/3)\Delta_D=O(D^{2/3})ΔD​=O(D2/3)

under the geometric hypotheses. It does not establish sharpness of the stronger minimum-diameter-vertex-cover bound in §44. The construction is nonlocal and nonglobal; its distinguished corner can move.

## 6. Summed corner costs and vertex cover (§44)

I find no algebraic error in the summed-corner argument.

Let KKK have perimeter PPP, area deficit at most CDCDCD, and let ωv\omega_vωv​ be its hull normal-cone angles. The angular intervals omitted by its unit tangent are disjoint. Applying the Fourier comparison simultaneously to their middle halves gives

J=P24π−area⁡(K)≥P2256π4∑vωv3.J=\frac{P^2}{4\pi}-\operatorname{area}(K) \ge\frac{P^2}{256\pi^4} \sum_v\omega_v^3.J=4πP2​−area(K)≥256π4P2​v∑​ωv3​.

Since J≤CDJ\le CDJ≤CD, and P2≥π2D2/2P^2\ge\pi^2D^2/2P2≥π2D2/2 for D≥8C/πD\ge8C/\piD≥8C/π,

∑vωv3≤512π2CD.\sum_v\omega_v^3\le\frac{512\pi^2C}{D}.v∑​ωv3​≤D512π2C​.

Let τ\tauτ be the minimum vertex cover of the actual diameter graph, not its total number of endpoints. Diameter-neighbor angular spacing gives

deg⁡D(v)≤1+Dωv.\deg_D(v)\le1+D\omega_v.degD​(v)≤1+Dωv​.

Hölder's inequality then yields

k≤τ+(512π2C)1/3D2/3τ2/3.k\le\tau+(512\pi^2C)^{1/3} D^{2/3}\tau^{2/3}.k≤τ+(512π2C)1/3D2/3τ2/3.

Combining with the triangle-free local-minimum input k≥D/2k\ge D/2k≥D/2 proves

τ=Ω(D).\boxed{\tau=\Omega(\sqrt D)}.τ=Ω(D​)​.

The constants and exponents check. This is stronger than using the maximum-degree estimate alone, but it remains a geometric covering-number result. It neither constructs a replacement region nor proves a contact-density bound.

The proposed Reuleaux-type sharpness of this vertex-cover exponent remains a separate, unverified construction. Section 41 proves sharpness of the maximum-degree exponent, not automatically of τ\tauτ.

## 7. The remaining structural and logical blockers

Eppstein's published result supplies four degree-two vertices in every biconnected triangle-free penny block. It supports §42's 4b0+3b14b_0+3b_14b0​+3b1​ count for blocks with zero or one articulation attachment. It does not support charging the same number to every block of an arbitrary block-cut tree. jgaa.info

The §45 two-form alternative is valid in its stated scope. Dines's rotation argument makes the joint image of two quadratic forms a convex cone; separating it from the open positive orthant produces a nonnegative dual combination. Three independent forms, or overlapping packet families with nonlinear cross terms, cannot be substituted without another argument.

Finally, the tie-breaker distinction has an exact algebraic explanation. At fixed β\betaβ, with no isolates,

M=β+n−c.M=\beta+n-c.M=β+n−c.

Thus minimizing M+qM+qM+q actually maximizes ccc when q=0q=0q=0. It cannot silently replace the ccc-minimizing normal form. Likewise, no argument here makes positive-stress edges interchangeable with all contacts, or actual diameter endpoints interchangeable with positively loaded endpoints.

The unresolved step is therefore concrete: establish a genuinely global rigidity, support-coverage or replacement principle that excludes the large detached trees and unrestricted branching frameworks still compatible with the verified necessary bounds. Neither M≥2n−O(D)M\ge2n-O(D)M≥2n−O(D) nor co-large adapted-stress support has been proved unconditionally.

Final assessment: §§32–45 provide meaningful conditional restrictions and explicit countermodels to tempting extensions. The cyclic-locking/Dines vacuity and incompatible tie-breakers are particularly important interactions. I found no justified route from these results to the universal eventual unit-triangle assertion. Erdős #99 remains unresolved.

Primary sources additionally include [Erdős (1994), §3.2](https://mathematica-pannonica.ttk.pte.hu/articles/mp05-2/mp05-2-261-269.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com), [Connelly–Demaine–Rote (2003)](https://erikdemaine.org/papers/Linkage/paper.pdf?utm_source=chatgpt.com) and [Eppstein (2018)](https://doi.org/10.7155/jgaa.00463?utm_source=chatgpt.com). # Erdős Problem 99: Bridge-rotation audit and a stronger bridge-chain obstruction

Verdict: The worker129 transverse-sign theorem is correct under its stated hypotheses, including the requirement that the bridge be in the complete unit-contact graph and that the configuration be selected to minimize the number of actual diameter pairs. The argument survives internal diameter pairs and zero-stress crossing diameters.

There is also a useful further obstruction: under a common positive equilibrium stress, a nonbranching chain of full-contact bridges with no internal diameter-active vertices must be geometrically straight, and its length is at most DDD. This gives a route toward controlling bbb, although it does not establish b=O(D)b=O(D)b=O(D).

## 1. Complete audit of worker129

Let P⊂R2P\subset\mathbb R^2P⊂R2 be finite, unit-separated, of diameter D>1D>1D>1. Assume:

- PPP globally minimizes diameter among configurations of its cardinality and, within the triangle-free global minimizers, lexicographically minimizes (β,c,k)(\beta,c,k)(β,c,k), with β=M−n+c\beta=M-n+cβ=M−n+c, MMM counting all unit contacts and kkk counting all actual diameter pairs.
- A full-contact bridge uvuvuv partitions P=S⊔TP=S\sqcup TP=S⊔T, with u∈Su\in Su∈S, v∈Tv\in Tv∈T, and no other unit contact crossing the cut.
- For nonnegative coefficients λpq\lambda_{pq}λpq​, and μ>0\mu>0μ>0, \[ \sum_{\substack{p\in S,\ q\in T\|p-q|=D}} \lambda_{pq}(p-q)=\mu e,\qquad e=u-v,\quad |e|=1. \tag{1} \]

The last identity is a hypothesis. It follows from a compatible global contact/diameter equilibrium stress assigning positive coefficient to uvuvuv, but a KKT condition alone does not guarantee that every full-contact bridge receives positive stress.

### Theorem: strict transverse sign diversity

For either unit normal w⊥ew\perp ew⊥e, there are actual crossing diameter vectors d+,d−d_+,d_-d+​,d−​, oriented from SSS to TTT, satisfying

d+⋅w>0,d−⋅w<0.(2)d_+\cdot w>0,\qquad d_-\cdot w<0. \tag{2}d+​⋅w>0,d−​⋅w<0.(2)

Proof. Suppose instead that all crossing actual diameter vectors satisfy d⋅w≥0d\cdot w\geq0d⋅w≥0.

Taking the www-component of (1), positivity of the coefficients implies that every positively stressed crossing diameter is parallel to eee. Taking the eee-component then yields at least one positively stressed vector d0=Ded_0=Ded0​=De. Importantly, this conclusion is existential; it does not assign positive longitudinal projection to other crossing diameters.

Write d0=p0−q0d_0=p_0-q_0d0​=p0​−q0​. The diameter constraint makes p0p_0p0​ and q0q_0q0​ the unique maximizer and minimizer, respectively, of projection onto eee. Indeed, another point attaining either extreme would be farther than DDD from the opposite endpoint.

Consequently every crossing actual diameter parallel to eee equals DeDeDe. The alternative −De-De−De would reverse the unique extremal endpoints, contradicting their membership in S,TS,TS,T.

Now fix SSS and translate TTT by

a(t)=(1−cos⁡t)e−sin⁡tw.a(t)=(1-\cos t)e-\sin t\,w.a(t)=(1−cost)e−sintw.

The bridge remains exactly unit length, since

u−(v+a(t))=cos⁡te+sin⁡tw.u-(v+a(t))=\cos t\,e+\sin t\,w.u−(v+a(t))=coste+sintw.

For each crossing diameter vector ddd,

∣d−a(t)∣2−D2=2(d⋅w)sin⁡t+2(d⋅e−1)(cos⁡t−1).(3)|d-a(t)|^2-D^2 =2(d\cdot w)\sin t +2(d\cdot e-1)(\cos t-1). \tag{3}∣d−a(t)∣2−D2=2(d⋅w)sint+2(d⋅e−1)(cost−1).(3)

Choose sufficiently small t<0t<0t<0.

If d⋅w>0d\cdot w>0d⋅w>0, its negative first-order contribution dominates the second-order term. If d⋅w=0d\cdot w=0d⋅w=0, the preceding uniqueness argument gives d=Ded=Ded=De, so

∣d−a(t)∣2−D2=2(D−1)(cos⁡t−1)<0.|d-a(t)|^2-D^2 =2(D-1)(\cos t-1)<0.∣d−a(t)∣2−D2=2(D−1)(cost−1)<0.

Thus every crossing actual diameter strictly shortens, including those carrying zero stress.

Previously subdiametral pairs remain below DDD by finite-gap continuity.

If no internal actual diameter exists, the entire configuration's diameter decreases, contradicting globality. Otherwise, its diameter remains DDD, but kkk strictly decreases.

In this second case, every original unit contact survives, no new one appears, and the partition remains linked by uvuvuv. Hence M,c,βM,c,\betaM,c,β remain unchanged, and the contact graph remains triangle-free. This contradicts lexicographic kkk-minimality.

We conclude that some crossing diameter has negative transverse projection. Repeating the argument with −w-w−w supplies a positive one. □\square□

### Scope checks

The proof does not require every crossing diameter to carry positive stress, every diameter to cross the bridge, or all crossing diameter vectors to have positive longitudinal projection.

Its essential requirements are the unique full-contact crossing, positive μ\muμ, common cut-equilibrium equation, D>1D>1D>1, and the permitted global kkk-minimizing selection.

In particular, replacing the full-contact bridge with a bridge only in the positive-stress subgraph is invalid: additional zero-stress unit contacts might be destroyed by the rotation.

The worker's theorem therefore passes this audit without implying ordinary local optimality from positive KKT stationarity alone.

## 2. Strengthening: conservation of diameter stress along bridge chains

The transverse-sign theorem constrains each bridge separately. A stronger conclusion follows when neighboring bridge cuts use one common global equilibrium stress.

### Proposition: stress-flux straightening

Assume a finite unit-separated configuration has one equilibrium stress satisfying, at every vertex xxx,

∑q:∣x−q∣=Dλxq(x−q)=∑y:∣x−y∣=1μxy(x−y),(4)\sum_{q:\,|x-q|=D}\lambda_{xq}(x-q) = \sum_{y:\,|x-y|=1}\mu_{xy}(x-y), \tag{4}q:∣x−q∣=D∑​λxq​(x−q)=y:∣x−y∣=1∑​μxy​(x−y),(4)

with all coefficients nonnegative.

Consider a sequence of full-contact bridges with positive coefficients μi\mu_iμi​. Suppose their corresponding cuts are nested and the intervening full-contact bridge-blocks contain no actual diameter endpoints.

Then all these bridges have the same oriented unit vector and the same positive stress coefficient.

In particular, if

x0,x1,…,xmx_0,x_1,\ldots,x_mx0​,x1​,…,xm​

is a path of positively stressed full-contact bridges whose internal vertices have full-contact degree two and are not actual diameter endpoints, then

and

m≤D.(5)\boxed{m\le D.} \tag{5}m≤D.​(5)

Proof. Orient consecutive cuts consistently, writing

Fi=∑diameters crossing cut iλpq(p−q)=μiei.F_i=\sum_{\text{diameters crossing cut }i}\lambda_{pq}(p-q) =\mu_i e_i.Fi​=diameters crossing cut i∑​λpq​(p−q)=μi​ei​.

Passing a cut across a bridge-block containing no diameter endpoint neither introduces nor removes any term in this sum. Hence Fi=Fi+1F_i=F_{i+1}Fi​=Fi+1​.

Because ∣ei∣=∣ei+1∣=1|e_i|=|e_{i+1}|=1∣ei​∣=∣ei+1​∣=1 and μi,μi+1>0\mu_i,\mu_{i+1}>0μi​,μi+1​>0,

μi=μi+1,ei=ei+1.\mu_i=\mu_{i+1},\qquad e_i=e_{i+1}.μi​=μi+1​,ei​=ei+1​.

When the intervening blocks are singleton vertices of full-contact degree two, consecutive bridge segments share endpoints. Their equal oriented vectors therefore concatenate into a straight unit-spaced path.

Its endpoints are separated by mmm, so m≤Dm\le Dm≤D. □\square□

The hypothesis that the coefficients come from one common stress is indispensable. Separate cut-equilibrium identities with unrelated choices of λ\lambdaλ do not imply conserved force vectors.

### Corollary: bends are diameter-loaded

At a full-contact degree-two vertex xxx, if both contacts have positive stress and their incident unit vectors are not opposite, equation (4) forces an incident actual diameter with positive coefficient.

# Erdős Problem 99: a spider-tree obstruction and an exact positive-stress countermodel

Main result. The leaf-forest obstruction extends to every connected unit-contact tree having at most one branching vertex, even when the actual-diameter graph contains an odd cycle.

More precisely, if every actual-diameter endpoint is a leaf of such a contact tree, ordinary local diameter minimality forces D≤2D\le 2D≤2.

The proof constructs an arbitrarily small feasible perturbation that strictly decreases every actual diameter. It requires neither positive stress nor infinitesimal rigidity.

There is also an exact family with arbitrarily large DDD, an actual-diameter triangle, and strictly positive equilibrium multipliers on every tree contact. Explicit second-order motions decrease its diameter. Thus these combinatorial and first-order conditions alone cannot establish a diameter bound.

Neither statement resolves the general branching-tree case or Erdős Problem 99, which remains listed as open. Erdős Problems

## 3. Consequences for the proposed obstruction

The result eliminates the entire requested conditional class, not merely its positive-stress core.

In particular:

- Nonleaf diameter endpoints are harmless. They may have several contact edges. The angular-speed construction satisfies all those edges simultaneously because their directed constraints belong to a forest.
- Zero-stress attachments are harmless. Every full contact edge is handled directly, whether or not it carries equilibrium stress.
- Ghost diameter pairs are harmless. Every antipodal boundary pair receives distinct angular speeds and contracts strictly.
- First-order stationarity is not an obstruction. Diameter pairs contract quadratically: \[ |p_i(t)-p_j(t)| =D-\frac D8(\omega_i-\omega_j)^2t^2+O(t^4). \] Hence zero first derivative of diameter is compatible with genuine strict descent.

A slightly more general sufficient condition also follows: the forest hypothesis can be replaced by acyclicity of the directed graph obtained after contracting opposite-ray radial contacts and orienting nonradial contacts according to their cross-product signs.

## 6. Interpretation for the cycle-and-spokes framework

The uploaded audit establishes an exact diameter-decreasing spoke rotation for its regular-cycle configuration, while its separate geometric lemma rules out every off-cycle double pin to that fixed regular cycle. The argument above supplies a broader, quantitative replacement for the latter fact.

| Frame or pinning situation | Rigorous conclusion |
| --- | --- |
| Regular unit cycle, k≥8k\ge8k≥8 | No off-cycle double pins in a triangle-free packing |
| Arbitrary strictly convex unit cycle, internally DDD-loaded, D≥16D\ge16D≥16 | At most 484812484\,812484812 off-cycle double-pinned points |
| Internally loaded cycle with strictly interior padding | Same bound, without further padding assumptions |
| Cycle vertices loaded only through off-cycle diameter partners | Uniform bound not established by this argument |
| Arbitrary coupled spoke networks | No general rigidity or descent conclusion |

There is an important distinction between two contacts directly to the frame and two contacts somewhere in a network attached to the frame.

The theorem limits the former, but permits a large network whose vertices each have only one direct frame contact and additional contacts among themselves. Such a network might obstruct the spoke rotation through collective second-order constraints.

Indeed, even zero double pins to the frame would not establish an admissible diameter descent for an arbitrary coupled spoke network.

The new bound therefore rules out an extensive direct-double-pinning strategy but does not exclude all possible stabilizing frameworks.

It also avoids two unsupported transfers highlighted in the research context:

- No area estimate for the positive-stress hull is transferred to the full packing hull.
- No positive-stress edge count is substituted for a count of all full unit contacts.

The proof is purely geometric.

## 7. Remaining gap toward Erdős 99

For the lexicographically selected triangle-free global optimizer described in the question, the established structural constraints include large-diameter contact components, tree structure outside the distinguished component, and lower bounds involving full-contact bridges.

The theorem here is conditional on a particularly strong substructure: a convex unit cycle whose every vertex has an actual diameter partner on that same cycle.

Those optimizer constraints do not imply the existence of such a cycle. Nor do they imply that all relevant contacts to a cyclic block must be direct double pins.

Consequently, the remaining bridge to the global conjecture would require a structural reduction producing an internally loaded convex unit cycle with sufficiently controlled attachments, or a different argument handling multi-hub networks, coupled single-pin spokes, and nonleaf diameter joints.

Neither follows from the bound above.

# Erdős 99: stress selection, forced ghosts, and the second-order obstruction

Conclusion: There is an exact first-order characterization of diameter edges and endpoints that cannot receive positive multipliers. It applies to full contact forests and, in fact, to arbitrary contact graphs. I also give a 10-point triangle-free configuration with a full contact tree in which an actual diameter edge has zero multiplier in every equilibrium.

That configuration is stationary but not an ordinary local minimum. Consequently, it does not settle either proposed assertion under ordinary local minimality.

The strongest conclusion established here is a first-order theorem together with a necessary second-order obstruction. Neither universal diameter-edge positivity nor universal endpoint coverage at ordinary local forest minima is proved or disproved.

The full eventual-unit-triangle conjecture remains open. Erdős Problems

## 2. Finite peeling exclusion theorem

Suppose additionally that the positive core TTT has a contact-length-preserving deformation that strictly decreases every actual diameter pair whose endpoints lie in TTT.

Each successful step eliminates at least one actual diameter equality and creates none. The positive core stays fixed.

There are finitely many diameter pairs, so the prescribed successful sequence terminates after finitely many steps.
